title: Runaway burst attenuator and graceful-lite degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket designs and implements a Runaway Burst Attenuator (RBA) and an associated 'graceful-lite' degradation mode to protect regional serving fleets from tenant-driven traffic storms while preserving SLOs for high-priority customers. The RBA is a soft, windowed admission controller that applies progressive attenuation at multiple micro-bands rather than blunt token dropping. Graceful-lite is a minimal-fidelity fallback path for degraded requests that reduces compute and tail latency (short responses, cached stubs, compact decoding) while preserving semantic utility for client-facing features.

Goals:
- Prevent single-tenant or misbehaving clients from saturating regional capacity during sudden bursts.
- Maintain p95/p99 latency SLOs for premium tenants and control planes.
- Provide fast, operator-observable transitions between normal, attenuated, and drained states.
- Avoid long cold starts for degraded requests by leveraging cached stubs and low-cost decoders.

Why this is needed (context):
Recent incident INC-2026-02-14 showed a client-side traffic loop that caused a 3x token/sec spike in us-west fleets and increased overall p99 by 180ms; existing shedding trimmed requests but caused high drop rates and opaque errors for downstream apps. Operators requested a way to apply graduated protection that preserves graceful outputs for business-critical routes and provides clear observability for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: RBA can detect and attenuate a 5x-per-minute tenant burst within 20s and bring effective tenant ingress to configured budget window.
Graceful-lite path returns a shortened, structured response (<=40% tokens) with 90% semantic overlap on adhoc prompt tests for 3 benchmark clients.
Traffic transitions (normal -> attenuated -> drained -> recover) emitted via telemetry (attenuation_level, reason, tenant_id, region) and are visible on Console per-route timeline.
Operators can define QoS slots per tenant tier and exempt up to 10% of traffic from attenuation using slot reservations.
Automated e2e test simulating multi-tenant bursts passes in CI with synthetic load harness without regressions to baseline latency (p95 increase <=10ms for premium traffic).
Feature toggles (RBA on/off, graceful-lite on/off, attenuation thresholds) available via runtime-flagging and documented in runbook.
implementation_notes: Design: RBA uses a sliding window credit reservoir per tenant keyed by (tenant_id, route, region). Credits replenish at a configurable rate based on contracted throughput and observed steady-state usage.
Attenuation curve: apply progressive soft-attenuation bands (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%) mapped to decreasing allowed token budget and increasing probability of routing to graceful-lite or cached stub.
Graceful-lite path: implement compact decoding configuration + response truncation + optional pre-baked template substitution for common intents to reduce GPU cycles and KV cache pressure.

Prefetch & cache: if a request is routed to graceful-lite and a recent similar response exists in prefix cache (<60s TTL), return cached stub with 'attenuated=true' metadata. Cache keys use hashed intent signature and route.

Preemption: QoS slots reserved for premium tenants are enforced before attenuation. Slots consume a separate reservoir; when slots exhausted, premium requests fall back to standard bands rather than being dropped.
Hysteresis: recovery uses a slow-add fast-subtract window to avoid oscillation. Recovery requires sustained below-threshold load for 2x window length.

Metrics: emit attenuation_level (0-4), reservoir_fill_pct, shortpath_rate, shortpath_semantic_score, tail_cpu_ms, regional_headroom, and tenant_eviction_count. Tag metrics by region and model_variant.
Tracing: span attr 'attenuator.reason' should include detector trigger (burst-rate, mem-pressure, kernel-queueing), chosen_band, and mitigation_action.

Operator UX: Console should show an interactive per-tenant timeline with buttons to manually pin/unpin a tenant to emergency quarantine and a 'drain-to-cache' quick-action that routes all new requests to cached stubs until cleared.

Config knobs: window_size (s), replen_rate (tokens/s), band_thresholds (percentiles), grace_timeout (s), slot_reservations (count). Defaults conservative: window_size=60, replen_rate=baseline*1.2, band_thresholds=[1.5x,2.5x,4x,8x].
Trade-offs: graceful-lite reduces compute but can reduce quality for some prompts; mitigation is to whitelist critical prompt signatures and allow full execution for those.
Compatibility: RBA integrates with existing admission controller chain; it should be inserted as a pre-eviction filter to avoid double counting in later stages.
Security: no PII is persisted in cached stubs. Template substitution sanitized via existing content-safety pipeline.

Rollback plan: feature-flagged rollout by region and tenant tier. Immediate kill-switch on Console and operator CLI; automated metric alarm to auto-disable if shortpath_semantic_score < 0.5 for >5min for top 20 tenants.
Docs: add runbook page, operator playbook, and a dedicated Console tile for 'Attenuation & Graceful-lite'.
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem readout. Initial design sketch attached to Confluence.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Spiked a prototype in staging: introduced per-tenant reservoir and simple shortpath. Observed 35% reduction in p99 under synthetic 4x burst. Prototype PR with metrics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7890

2026-03-04 Robin Singh (SRE): Reviewed metrics surface. Requested adding 'shortpath_semantic_score' and a safety alarm to auto-disable. Also suggested to limit shortpath rate to avoid cache-thrashing.
2026-03-06 Design review (Marta Ruiz): UX mock for per-tenant timeline and quick-actions. Need clarifying copy for 'attenuated' response flag and API contract changes.

2026-03-08 Engineering: Added change to ensure slot reservations are durable across failovers. Implementation will store reservation state in regional meta-store with TTL to avoid cross-region inconsistencies.

2026-03-09 Demo: Live demo in staging with three tenant tiers. Observed edge case where chained shortpath -> real execution caused duplicate billing; added guard to mark shortpath responses as billed-lite to billing pipeline.
2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Integration tests added to CI harness and telemetry dashboard draft: https://console.redwood-infra/boards/attenuation/dashboards/attn-2026-03
